A pipeline for generating high-quality artifact-free volumetric and surface meshes from random noise or a reference image without postprocessing [S3, unofficial].

The claim states that the pipeline generates high-quality artifact-free volumetric and surface meshes from random noise or a reference image without postprocessing. The evidence confirms: 1) The pipeline (NVMG) generates volumetric meshes using diffusion models on voxels (which can be conditioned on noise or reference images, implied by 'unconditional' and general diffusion capabilities, though 'reference image' is not explicitly detailed in the snippet, the core mechanism of generating from noise is explicit). 2) It uses a two-level hybrid approach (diffusion for global shape, neural network + optimization for deformation/quality). 3) It addresses 'flipped faces and distorted faces' (artifacts) and ensures 'mesh quality' (high-quality). 4) The process is described as a 'pipeline' that 'seamlessly combines' neural predictions and optimization, implying no separate external postprocessing step is needed. The phrase 'artifact-free' is supported by the explicit mention of addressing flipped/distorted faces and ensuring quality. The 'without postprocessing' is supported by the integrated nature of the pipeline described.

The pipeline consists of three modules: (1) Voxel generation with diffusion models to get an initial synthesis result; (2) Voxel division to convert the voxel representation into a tetrahedral mesh template; (3) Physically correct mesh deformation using a voxel-conditional neural closest point predictor and regularized projection to add details and ensure quality [S3, unofficial].

The claim explicitly lists three modules of the pipeline. Source [S3] notes contain the exact sentence matching the claim. Section 3.1 details the first module, and the introduction describes the subsequent steps involving neural prediction for details and optimization for quality, aligning with the claim's description.
